_what_this_is: THE STACK-SPECIFIC HALF OF THE HARNESS, in one file.
`ci.py` is the step ladder: run each rung in order, print a positive marker with a
count, name the rung that stopped the run. That part IS the same in every factory -
two people built it independently and wrote the same file.
What is NOT the same is every command it runs. The first version of this scaffold
hardcoded `python -m compileall` and `python -m unittest`, which made a template
claiming to be universal quietly Python-only. The commands live here instead.
Set what you have. Leave a step empty and it is SKIPPED LOUDLY - the log says
<STEP>_SKIPPED and the gate can be told to require the marker, so a skipped rung is
never mistaken for a passed one.
_unit_count_pattern: A regex with ONE group that captures how many tests ran. Zero is not a pass: a suite that discovered nothing exits 0 and looks perfect. Leave empty to skip the count check, and accept that you cannot tell a passing suite from an absent one.
_driver: How the E2E reaches your software. THREE SHAPES cover almost everything:
http     a server. Started on a dynamic port, polled until healthy.
cli      a command. Invoked with args, stdout/stderr asserted.
library  no process at all. The E2E imports and calls it.
A frontend app is `http` plus a browser-automation CLI in your e2e.py.

cli._note: The command under test. {args} is substituted per call from e2e.py.

library._note: Nothing to start. APP_STARTED is emitted after this import succeeds, which is the equivalent proof that the thing loads at all.

browser._note: ONLY for an app whose correctness is visual. Leave install_check empty if e2e.py never drives a browser. When it is set, factory_doctor runs it at setup - so a missing browser is a setup failure with an install command, not a mystery hang at gate time on a fresh runner.
browser.install_hint: npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install   |   pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
